name: Zenithal-Bergschrund
description: A shell of ancient ice seals the world, cracked into plates the size of nations and refrozen in place. Pressure ridges stack in turquoise ramparts, gleaming under a stingy sun near ancient meteor crater.
The air carries ozone and crushed stone, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
Survey contracts pay double for reasons nobody writes down. Veterans read the fine print, then read the survivors.
